subject.title: Anthropic setup-token onboarding path has multiple failure modes (docs gap, credential propagation, multi-agent sync)

question: Should Anthropic setup-token/manual-token auth rely on runtime read-through, copy portable static token profiles to sibling agent stores, or use a different explicit operator-controlled sync path?
rationale: The remaining fix can change where sensitive provider credentials live and whether agent stores inherit or receive copied token material, so automation should not choose the credential boundary without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Prefer read-through plus validation/docs
options.body: Keep runtime inheritance as the default, add clearer setup-token guidance and post-write/status validation, and avoid copying credentials unless an explicit sync path is approved.

options.title: Approve static-token sibling sync
options.body: Allow a narrow sync path for portable Anthropic token profiles while preserving OAuth non-portability and adding focused tests for all setup-token, paste-token, and non-interactive surfaces.

options.title: Close as mitigated
options.body: Treat runtime read-through as sufficient and close this after closing or superseding the linked fix PR, accepting that prompt clarity and validation remain separate follow-ups.

recommendation.title: Prefer read-through plus validation/docs
recommendation.body: Keep runtime inheritance as the default, add clearer setup-token guidance and post-write/status validation, and avoid copying credentials unless an explicit sync path is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history on the auth read-through contract and the current affected auth-store boundaries.
